   Vernon Housing Commission Agenda Report

Meeting Date:  September 13, 2023
From:  Lisa Pope, City Clerk
Department:  City Clerk
Submitted by:  Sandra Dolson, Administrative Secretary

Subject
Selection of Chair and Vice Chair

Recommendation
Select one member to serve as Chair and one member to serve as Vice Chair for the term ending
June 30, 2024.

Background
The Vernon Housing Commission consists of seven members, including three residents (one
member of the City Council), three business representatives, and one employee of a Vernon
business. Members serve four-year terms, serving no more than two consecutive, full four-year
terms.

The current members are as follows:

Commissioner  Appointing Category  Date Appointed End of Term
Juliet Goff  Business Representative  July 20, 2021  June 30, 2025
Ronit Edry  Business Representative  June 6, 2023  June 30, 2027
Jorge Nevarez Jr.  Business Representative  June 6, 2023  June 30, 2027
Bertha Padilla  Employee of a Business  June 6, 2023  June 30, 2027
Steven Froberg  Resident  July 20, 2021  June 30, 2025
Leticia Lopez  Resident (Council Member) July 20, 2021  June 30, 2025
Marlene Ybarra  Resident  June 6, 2023  June 30, 2027

Municipal Code Section 2.40.050 requires a Chairperson and Vice Chairperson from different
appointing categories and prohibits a member from serving as Chair for more than two (2)
consecutive terms.

Chair Goff was appointed as Chairperson on September 14, 2022, serving one consecutive
term; therefore, she is eligible to continue to serve as Chair if the Commission so determines.
Additionally, all other Commissioners are eligible to serve as Chair

The Commission should select a Chair and Vice Chair to serve through June 30, 2024.

Fiscal Impact
There is no fiscal impact associated with this report.

Attachments
None.

  City Clerk Pope presented the staff report and conducted the housing lotteries to

 Special Vernon Housing Commission Meeting Minutes  Page 2 of 3
July 12, 2023

PRESENTATIONS

1.  Amending Title 17 of the Municipal Code and General Plan to Allow Mixed
  Use Industrial Zoning in Four Districts

  Commissioner Ybarra indicated she had a conflict of interest due to her property
  interest in the City and would recuse herself.

  Commissioner Ybarra left the dais at 6:10 p.m.

  Public Works Director Wall presented the staff report.

  In response to Commission questions, Public Works Director Wall explained the
  environmental impact report, which included traffic studies; stakeholder group of
  17 members, including business owners; public notification provided; and
  proposed live workspace.

MOTION
  Commissioner Edry moved to mail notices to businesses separate from utility bills.
  The motion died due to lack of a second.

MOTION
  Chair Goff moved and Commissioner Padilla seconded a motion to receive the
  presentation and recommend that the Council adopt amendments allowing Mixed
  Use Industrial Zoning in four districts. The question was called and the motion
  carried 4-0, (Vice Chair Nevarez, and Commissioners Froberg and Ybarra absent).

  Commissioner Ybarra returned to the dais at 6:37 p.m.

ORAL REPORTS

2.  Brief Reports, Announcements, or Directives to Staff

  Administrative Analyst Figueroa reported on the Department of Toxic Substances
  Control (DTSC) lead remediation of soil at Vernon Village Park Apartments and at
  the City owned home on Vernon Avenue and its plans to distribute reimbursement
  checks to residents that had relocated; and on the City’s successful Summer Swim
  community outreach event at the Southeast Rio Vista YMCA.
